_doc: Configuration of the benchmark matrix. 'indexes' says what tools/build_db.py puts into a corpus database; 'configs' says how bench/matrix.py queries it. A config runs only if its index is present in the database manifest, so a new layout drops in by adding one index entry and its configs. Values under 'per_corpus' override an index's params for that corpus. SQL uses named parameters :q (query text or float32 blob) and :k; {table} is the index's table name.

fts.desc: FTS5 external-content index over docs(body), unicode61 tokenizer, 'optimize'd

dense_graph.params: dim=384, layout=colocated, vectors=inline, store_vectors=f16, M=16, ef_construction=200, threads=2, codebook=int8
dense_graph.desc: HNSW-built layer-0 graph, int8 PQ codebook, co-located PQ-64 neighbour codes, inline float16 vectors, page hints

dense_ivf.params: dim=384, layout=ivf, store_vectors=f16, threads=2, ivf_centroids=auto, codebook=int8
dense_ivf.desc: IVF-PQ (IVFADC, PQ-64 residual codes, int8 codebook), nlist = 4 sqrt(N), int8 centroids below 1,024 lists (PQ above), float16 vectors in a table for reranking

late.params: dim=48 nbits=2 centroids=0 layout=both order=1 threads=2 input=f16 centroid_type=int8

per_corpus.words-1m: layout=warp nbits=2 centroids=65536 fast_assign=1 sample_tokens=2000000 mem_mb=1024 centroid_type=int8

late.desc: LateOn-Code-edge token vectors, 2-bit residuals, K = fast-plaid formula (65,536 at 1M), int8 centroids, warp postings + plaid rows + IVF

configs.label: FTS5 bm25 (AND)
configs.sql: SELECT rowid AS id FROM {table} WHERE {table} MATCH :q ORDER BY rank LIMIT :k

configs.label: FTS5 bm25 (OR)
configs.sql: SELECT rowid AS id FROM {table} WHERE {table} MATCH :q ORDER BY rank LIMIT :k

configs.label: FTS5 bm25c (OR)
configs.sql: SELECT rowid AS id FROM {table} WHERE {table} MATCH :q AND rank MATCH 'bm25c()' ORDER BY rank LIMIT :k

configs.label: FTS5 unranked (AND)
configs.sql: SELECT rowid AS id FROM {table} WHERE {table} MATCH :q LIMIT :k
